Gullible

/GUL-uh-bul/ — stress on GUL · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is gullible believes things too easily and can be tricked or fooled without much effort.

Marcus was so gullible that he believed the cafeteria was serving 'invisible soup' on April first.

Worked Example

The con artist targeted gullible tourists at the airport, convincing them that his 'discount jewelry' was genuine.

Gull (trick, an old English verb) + -ible (can be done) = able to be tricked. The con artist's targeting of these travelers works precisely because they are susceptible to deception — they can be easily gulled or fooled.

How Gullible Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

credulous

credulous: too ready to believe what is merely said; gullible goes further - so easily fooled that tricksters can take you in

naive

naive: innocently lacking experience and judgment

trusting

trusting: inclined to assume others are honest

Antonyms

skeptical

skeptical: doubting claims until proof appears

wary

wary: cautious and on guard against tricks

How Strong Is It? — accepting → trusting → unsuspecting → gullible

accepting vs. gullible

accepting vs. gullible: An accepting listener takes your story at face value, while a gullible one would believe it even with obvious holes in it.

trusting vs. gullible

trusting vs. gullible: A trusting friend assumes you mean well, but a gullible one believes even your most outrageous claims.

unsuspecting vs. gullible

unsuspecting vs. gullible: An unsuspecting customer simply isn't looking for a scam, while a gullible one falls for the scam even after the warning signs appear.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — gull

Root — gull: to trick or deceive — a rare old English verb; not the seabird, which today is best treated as a separate word with the same spelling (English (deeper origin uncertain))

Suffix — -ible

Suffix — -ible: able to be; capable of being (Latin (-ibilis))

Put it together

Put it together: gull ('to trick') + -ible = able to be tricked — someone who believes things too easily. Watch the homograph trap: this gull is a rare old verb meaning 'to deceive,' not the seabird — the bird meaning of gull will not help you decode gullible, even though the two words are spelled exactly the same.

Use the root in a new word: gullibility

Use the root in a new word: gullibility: The scam artist counted on the gullibility of his victims to make the fake prize seem real.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral; slightly informal

Gullible describes someone who is easily deceived or fooled — too quick to believe without questioning. Use it to show that a character's naiveté or lack of caution makes them vulnerable to manipulation.
